correctness.rationale: Every singleton is blocked because the initial white graph is connected and the unique blue vertex has at least two white neighbors. Each listed pair has an explicit valid componentwise PSD forcing sequence. Every unlisted two-set consists of page vertices on distinct pages; its white graph is connected and each blue page vertex has both cycle-neighbors white, so no first PSD force is possible. These cases exhaust all pairs. A standard-library verifier independently checks every singleton and pair for \(1\le n\le12\); the finite computation is corroborative, not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: Book graphs are a standard named family used in PSD zero forcing as an edge-contraction example. The prior scalar \(Z_+=2\) does not determine optimal placements. The complete classification and count \(5n+1\) resolve that natural missing finite structure, distinguishing the spine pair, same-page pairs, and all spine-page pairs. This is a motivated exact classification of optimal configurations rather than a routine restatement of the known minimum number.
